label: Claude Opus 5.5
output:
Hey Mikaela, no worries at all, happy to give you the real version. You were there for us when Dave did his shoulder, so I'm not going to sell you anything!

We've got 290, mostly 3-way crossbreds, and we started 10 in 7 on 21 Sept once mating had kicked off. We skip the Tues, Thurs, Sat and Sun arvo milkings, so it's 4 once-a-days a week. Mornings are 5.15 every day. We're only about 7 weeks in, so keep that in mind.

Production: milksolids are down about 6% on the same weeks last year, going off the Fonterra app. Our rep had told us to expect 8-10%, so it's been better than we were warned. Still a hit though, and you'd need to run your own numbers on what 6% means for you.

Cells: yes, they jumped. We went from 110k to about 180k in the first 3 weeks, which gave me a bit of a fright. They've come back to around 135k now but haven't got back to where we were. I'll be honest, we had a heifer with mastitis go bad on a skipped arvo. We didn't spot her till the next morning and she lost a quarter. That one's on us, and it's the big lesson. You have to be on your game with teat spraying and actually walking through and checking the cows on the skip days. If you get slack it bites you, and it bites fast.

The cows came round quicker than I expected. They had about 4 days of bellowing at the gate on the skipped arvos and then they were fine. That's not saying yours will be the same, but it wasn't the drama I was bracing for.

Lameness has been the surprise good bit. We've got 4 on the lame list now compared to 11 this time last year. Our long walk to the back paddocks is 1.8km, so having fewer trips down the race has made a real difference.

The people side is where it's really paid off for us. The first skipped Sunday arvo, Dave and I drove to Hamilton to see the grandkids. That was our first Sunday off in spring in 20-odd years. Kieran, our 2IC, said it's the first spring he hasn't wanted to quit by October. With your young fella already talking about leaving, I'd say that's probably the strongest argument for it. And if Tom's knees are bad, having the arvos off will help him more than anything else will.

Would I go back? Honestly no. The hours alone are worth the 6% to us. But I don't want you going in thinking it's free, because it isn't. You lose some milk, the cells will likely go up for a bit, and you can't drop the ball on animal checks. If your vet's keen, get them involved early around cell counts and what to watch for.

Come and have a look at our shed rosters and numbers at the field day on the 19th, I'll bring them along. Grant, same goes for you if you're thinking about it again.

And ring me if you like, it's way easier than me trying to type all this with my thumbs 😂

Bev
